analysis: The PR changes only CHANGELOG.md (patch hunks at old/new lines ~107-126). There is no source, so it alters no runtime security behavior. The added entries describe account-erasure behavior that lives elsewhere (T-059, TB-006, TB-008). First entry: cancel restores only credentials recorded as live at confirm (schema v34, `erasure_revoked_credentials`) and not revoked during the grace period. Second: a Privy user ID in erasure cannot create a new account until the outbox has deleted the Privy user (schema v33 `privy_user` outbox row). Third: a late rejection record of an erased account keeps no model names or parameters. Fourth: `PUT /v1/pricing` returns 409 `account_deleted` from confirm onward. Also described: scrub of API key model lists, App Attest shadow events, revocation reasons, Stripe failure reasons, payment tx hashes/memos, provider model prices and wallet hash. The line 123 change now says login stays blocked until the Privy user is deleted. These are claimed mitigations for erased-account data remnants, credential resurrection on cancel, and identity re-binding. The changelog does not verify them, and no code was supplied. The next pass must check the real Go store/API code against these claims. Check that cancel cannot resurrect credentials revoked for security reasons (the revoked-during-grace exclusion). Check that the Privy deletion worker never deletes a Privy user held by a live account, and that a deleted-Privy token returns 401. Check that the pricing 409 gate is enforced in both memory and PostgreSQL stores. T-059 (oversized, not visible) may need its description updated to cover the new scrub fields and Privy outbox behavior. No threat-model assumption is invalidated by the changelog text alone.
